about.title: Rancho Mirage Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Riverside County recorded 3 traffic deaths in Rancho Mirage in the most recent final crash year, alongside 84 injury collisions and 113 people hurt on local roads. Behind each of those numbers is a family trying to make sense of a sudden loss. Corridors like Bob Hope Drive, Highway 111, Rt 111, and Dinah Shore Drive see steady traffic volume, and public crash data shows Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. as a common time for reported collisions. If a crash on one of these roads took the life of your spouse, partner, parent, or child, California law gives certain family members and dependents the right to pursue a wrongful death claim. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves — we simply connect grieving families in Rancho Mirage with an independent personal injury attorney who handles these cases on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless money is recovered. Reaching out costs nothing and starts with a conversation, not a commitment.

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing primarily to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children, with certain other dependents and heirs eligible in specific circumstances. An independent attorney can help sort out who in your family qualifies before any claim moves forward.

items.title: A Firm Two-Year Window
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though a claim against a government entity carries a much shorter deadline. Because Rancho Mirage roads include public thoroughfares, it's worth confirming timing early rather than assuming there's no rush.

items.title: Losses That Go Beyond the Funeral Bill
items.desc: California law recognizes recoverable losses including funeral and burial costs, lost financial support the deceased would have provided, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. These are separate considerations from any criminal case that may arise from the same incident.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, California law allows two years from the date of death to bring a wrongful death claim. If the claim involves a government entity, such as a public road or municipal vehicle, the deadline is much shorter and requires prompt action. An independent attorney can confirm the exact timeline based on the facts of your case.

items.question: Can extended family or a domestic partner file a claim, or only a spouse and children?
items.answer: California prioritizes a surviving spouse, domestic partner, and children as the primary parties with standing to file. If none of those exist, certain other dependents or heirs may be eligible under specific circumstances. This is one of the first things an independent attorney will help clarify for your family.

items.question: Does a wrongful death claim depend on a criminal case being filed first?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal charges that may result from a fatal crash on a road like Bob Hope Drive or Highway 111. The civil case can proceed on its own timeline regardless of whether criminal charges are filed, dropped, or resolved.
